summary: edit_file now follows pi edit-diff semantics via tools::apply_text_edit (shared by approval preview and invoke): strips a leading UTF-8 BOM (kept on write), matches on LF-normalized text (CRLF and lone CR), prefers an exact match and falls back to a fuzzy match (per-line trailing whitespace ignored; Unicode single/double quotes, dashes/minus, NBSP and Unicode spaces, ellipsis and full-width ASCII folded to ASCII as an NFKC subset, no new deps). Uniqueness is judged on the fuzzy form; 0 or >1 matches are rejected with 'old text must occur exactly once (found N)' plus a hint. Unlike pi, a position map (NormalizedText) rewrites only the matched source span, so the rest of the file keeps its bytes, and `new` is written with the file's line ending (CRLF stays CRLF). Tool description updated.

notes: tests/tools.rs reliability_line_ending_diff_is_exact_and_can_be_applied used edit_file to convert a whole file's line endings; that contradicts pi semantics (new text is written with the file's ending), so its edit cases now assert CRLF preservation for partial edits while write_file keeps the verbatim line-ending cases.
